title: CLO 2026.0 - Materials
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! CLO technical experts provide a detailed explanation of material-related feature updates: selecting materials when opening fabrics & swapping front and back materials, optimizing the fabric editor, and customizing notches.
transcript:
In version 2026.0, the process of opening ZFAB files has been optimized to allow selecting functions for different materials and attributes, enabling correct material changes.  
In the previous version, pressing the Ctrl key while dragging the fabric to the object window allowed loading different materials and attributes.  
In version 2026.0, this function has been optimized for a better experience.  
First, select the fabric in the object window.  
In the property editor, click the button to open the fabric.  
In the tab, select Open, then choose Material.  
In the folder, select the fabric file and click Open.  
In the window where the fabric is opened, you can assign the front, back, and side of the fabric.  
Choose whether to open the selected material or physical attribute.  
You can opt to only add the front fabric and deselect the reverse fabric.  
Click OK.  
You can observe the effect in the 3D window.  
The front and side fabrics are updated.  
The reverse fabric retains the original fabric settings.  
Open the simulation to check the physical properties of the material.  
In the property editor, the fabric is located on the right side under the side-switch label.  
A new exchange has been added to the back material button.  
Press the left button.  
In the 3D window, you can see that the front and back fabrics match each other.  
Switch to the reverse if the hook uses the same material on the front.  
At this point, the button to switch between front and back material disappears.  
The cancel hook option reappears.  
Through this update, when opening a GFAB file,  
users can quickly open the required part and switch between front and back materials with one click.  

In version 2026.0,  
we optimized the user interface and size adjustment behavior of the GFAB editor,  
providing a more concise user interface and a more convenient workflow.  
Let’s review the interface and editing process after the update.  
In the previous version,  
when processing a custom GFAB,  
properties such as rough line thickness, the number of rows per inch, and fabric thickness were displayed directly in the property editor and could be edited directly.  
In the latest update,  
these specific options have been removed from the property editor.  
To modify these values,  
you need to enter the GFAB editor.  
After removing these parameters,  
the property editor’s current property list is more concise,  
and detailed needle parameters are specifically managed within the GFAB editor.  
If you want to adjust the size of the GFAB,  
you can use the GFAB loop in the upper right corner of the GFAB editor.  
You can also adjust the GFAB loop function.  
After adjusting the number of rows and horizontal lines,  
you can click the button to adjust the size of the GFAB loop.  
More importantly,  
during this process,  
your existing needle design will be fully preserved.  
Additionally,  
if you need to completely reset the design content,  
a reset status button has been added to the window in the lower left corner.  
Clicking this button will immediately reset all needles in the window to default needles,  
allowing you to start designing anew.  
The GFAB editor update in version 2026.0  
provides a more focused and efficient environment for needle design.  

Furthermore,  
the GFAB editor received another update.  
In version 2026.0,  
we expanded the reset and recovery functions to the GFAB editor,  
enabling a more flexible and efficient editing process.  
You can use the main menu,  
navigate to Edit,  
Cancel,  
and Restore to use these commands.  
For a more efficient workflow,  
these commands can now also be used directly within the GFAB editor operations.  
Press Ctrl + Z to undo.  
Press Ctrl + Y to redo.  
After editing the needle design or parameters,  
you can use shortcut keys to immediately revert to the previous state or redo changes.  
This new function makes the design process more convenient,  
allowing you to easily try different needle structures  
and quickly modify any changes.  

In version 2026.0,  
the 3D zipper supports custom zippers.  
First, adjust the custom zipper OBJ file to the appropriate size and position.  
The zipper size is adjusted according to the actual zipper size.  
The zipper position must be ensured on both sides.  
The zipper overlap position is located at the coordinate point.  
We can copy it,  
paste it,  
and place the zipper overlap on both sides.  
Then delete one side’s zipper.  
Delete a zipper by defining the OBJ.  
Select the file to delete OBJ.  
After the delete OBJ dialog box appears,  
click OK.  
In the main menu bar,  
go to Material > UV > Zipper > Custom OBJ  
to open the custom zipper window.  
You can also click on the zipper in the object window,  
locate the zipper in the property editor below,  
and click the plus sign on the right to customize the zipper operation.  
In the displayed dialog box,  
change the name of the zipper.  
Add the zipper OBJ file,  
and you can view the effect in the window view within the browser.  
Adjust the zipper direction appropriately.  
Click to confirm that the customized zipper is complete.  
This new function helps you customize various zippers.

chunks.content: ## Material Loading and Assignment in CLO 2026.0 This section explains the optimized process for opening and assigning fabrics and materials in CLO 2026.0, detailing how to selectively load front, back, and side fabric attributes with improved workflow controls. In CLO version 2026.0, the process of opening ZFAB files has been optimized to allow users to select specific functions for different materials and attributes, enabling accurate material changes. Previously, pressing the Ctrl key while dragging fabric to the object window allowed loading different materials and attributes, but this function has been enhanced for a smoother experience. ### Procedure for Opening Fabrics 1. Select the fabric in the object window. 2. In the property editor, click the button to open the fabric. 3. In the tab, select **Open** then choose **Material**. 4. Navigate to the folder, select the fabric file, and click **Open**. 5. In the fabric open window, assign the front, back, and side fabrics as needed. 6. Choose whether to open the selected material or the physical attribute. 7. Optionally, add only the front fabric and deselect the reverse fabric. 8. Click **OK**. The 3D window updates to reflect changes, showing the front and side fabrics updated while the reverse fabric retains its original settings. ### Viewing and Switching Materials - Open the simulation to check the physical properties of the material. - The fabric properties appear under the side-switch label in the property editor on the right. - A new button allows exchanging the back material. - Press the left button to see the front and back fabrics matched in the 3D window. - Switch to the reverse fabric if the hook uses the same material on the front. - Once switched, the button to toggle between front and back materials disappears, and the cancel hook option reappears. This update enables users to quickly open required parts of a GFAB file and switch between front and back materials with a single click, improving workflow efficiency. --- ## GFAB Editor Interface and Size Adjustment Updates This section covers the user interface improvements and enhanced control over needle design parameters in the GFAB editor within CLO 2026.0, including how to adjust fabric parameters and loop sizes. Version 2026.0 introduces a more concise user interface and improved size adjustment behavior for the GFAB editor, streamlining the editing process. ### Changes to Property Editor and Parameter Management - Previously, parameters such as rough line thickness, number of rows per inch, and fabric thickness were editable directly in the property editor. - These specific options have been removed from the property editor in 2026.0. - To modify these values, users now must enter the GFAB editor. - This change results in a cleaner property editor list while centralizing detailed needle parameters within the GFAB editor. ### Size Adjustment Workflow - Use the GFAB loop control in the upper right corner of the GFAB editor to adjust size. - Adjust the number of rows and horizontal lines as required.

Overall, these updates create a more focused and efficient environment for needle design within the GFAB editor. --- ## Undo and Redo Functionality in GFAB Editor This section describes the expanded reset, undo, and redo functions in the GFAB editor, improving flexibility and efficiency during needle design and parameter editing. In CLO 2026.0, the GFAB editor has enhanced reset and recovery capabilities: - Undo and redo commands are accessible via the main menu: **Edit > Cancel** and **Edit > Restore**. - These commands can now also be used directly within the GFAB editor operations. - Keyboard shortcuts are supported: - **Ctrl + Z** for undo - **Ctrl + Y** for redo After editing needle designs or parameters, users can quickly revert changes or redo actions using these shortcuts, streamlining experimentation with different needle structures and speeding up modifications. --- ## Custom Zipper Support in CLO 2026.0 This section details the new support for custom zippers in 3D simulations, including how to import, position, and customize zipper OBJ files. Version 2026.0 adds support for custom zippers in the 3D zipper system. ### Preparing Custom Zipper OBJ Files - Adjust the custom zipper OBJ file to the correct size and position based on the actual zipper dimensions. - Ensure zipper placement on both sides aligns correctly. - The zipper overlap position should be set at a specific coordinate point. - Copy and paste the zipper overlap to both sides. - Delete one side's zipper OBJ by defining the OBJ to delete: 1. Select the file to delete OBJ. 2. Confirm deletion in the dialog box. ### Importing and Customizing Zippers - Access the custom zipper window via the main menu: **Material > UV > Zipper > Custom OBJ**. - Alternatively, select the zipper in the object window, locate it in the property editor, and click the plus sign to customize. - In the customization dialog box: - Rename the zipper. - Add the zipper OBJ file. - Preview the zipper effect in the browser window. - Adjust zipper direction as needed. - Confirm completion by clicking OK.
